# Dynamic Release Checklist

This site turns a list of questions and conditional tasks into a checklist that shows only the items that apply.

Public pages are served from this repository, often under https://www.clickthisnick.com/dynamic-release-checklist/ .

## What an agent should follow

Follow only the applicable items. On a checklist page that list is the text of `#applicable-checklist-text`, inside the collapsed `<details id="applicable">`. It stays in the DOM when the section is closed. Checkbox labels in `#tasks-root` are the short human wording for those same items. A safety note on an item is visually hidden text inside its label and is also written after the short line in `#applicable-checklist-text` and in `checklist.txt`.

Do not treat `tasks.json`, or the JSON inside `#checklist-data`, as a flat list of instructions. Those files contain every branch, including tasks that do not apply to the current answers.

Tasks that do not apply are omitted from the page. They are not hidden with CSS.

## How to use a checklist

1. Open an example, for example `examples/travel-checklist/checklist.html`.
2. Read the safety notice `#safety-notice` at the top. It is always visible.
3. Answer each question with the Yes or No choice. The question text is the paragraph next to those choices.
4. Read `#applicable-checklist-text` for the plain-text list, including any safety note after a short item. `#applicable-summary` says how many items apply.
5. Open the Checklist tab to check items off. The tab buttons are labeled Questions, Roles, and Checklist. A checked item has visually hidden text "Completed." The visible label stays the short task.
6. The page URL stores `answers` (question id to true or false), `view`, and `done` (indexes of checked tasks). `redirectToTasks=true` opens the Checklist tab.

Each checklist also links to `checklist.txt`, a plain-text copy of the conditional rules, plus `questions.json` and `tasks.json`.

## Safety

Never tell a person to turn off, unplug, or disable a smoke alarm or a carbon monoxide alarm. The safety notice says to leave them on and plugged in. Phone alarms are reminders on a phone. "Turn off air conditioners and heaters" and "Unplug nonessential electronics" apply only when the house-empty question is Yes. Their notes say to leave smoke and CO alarms on and not to unplug them or the refrigerator. "Unplug the window shade" is the window shade.

## Build

From the repository root, run `node scripts/build.js`. That refreshes the static checklist.html and checklist.txt files. Node.js 18 or newer is required. Then run `node scripts/serve.js` and open the local index. Opening a published checklist does not run a build.
